# TrustSQL: Benchmarking Text-to-SQL Reliability with Penalty-Based Scoring

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#trustsql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.15879v6) · arXiv:2403.15879v6, 2 July 2024

**Reading coverage:** All 28 PDF pages: Sections 1-7, Supplementary A–I, scoring equations, Tables 1-13, diagrams/captions, threshold procedure and datasheet.

## Research question

Evaluate SQL generation together with abstention when requests exceed a schema or a declared SQL-only task boundary.

## Method

Combines feasible questions with five infeasible categories and assigns rewards/penalties to correct SQL, wrong SQL and abstention. Pipeline and unified baselines use classifiers, judges, uncertainty thresholds or unanimous sampling.

## Evaluation

ATIS, Advising, EHRSQL and Spider; test sets contain equal feasible/infeasible counts. Domain-specific splits mix seen and unseen SQL structures, while Spider holds out databases. Ambiguity resolution is explicitly excluded.

## What the results support

Increasing penalties changes method rankings and strongly rewards conservative answering. Always abstaining scores 50% at every penalty; one reported setting answers just one correct Spider question and abstains on the rest.

## Limits and qualifications

Positive reliability scores reflect the benchmark's utility choices, prevalence and penalty, not demonstrated deployment safety. Non-SQL labels depend on allowed functionality. Preprocessing removes null/empty results and rewrites context assumptions, limiting realism.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A clear joint answer-or-abstain protocol; report coverage and error types beside its score and do not treat it as a clarification benchmark.
